head: 07481358c2d7ccba6c2a85f1c11e288d3a825a1b
summary: I set SL-038's O-030 from done:true to done:false in .taad/slices/SL-038/build-slice-2.json. The edit is anchored on the "key": "O-030" line. It is a one-line diff (numstat 1 1), CRLF is kept, no BOM was added, and the how-text is byte-identical. I added O-030, owed to the person, to the record the person's network check works from: the 'person-run network check' in docs/design/SL-020-scanner.md, next to N-001..N-004. The entry gives the exact command and the ~70 s run time, says the record there is where O-030 gets discharged, and says SL-038's O-030 stays done:false as history. It also records that spike#55's 66.2 s agent pass broke the rule that no stage runs this check, and that the pass does not discharge O-030. I added tests/bugs/SL-062-LedgerCases.ps1, which only reads files and git (cases C-002..C-005). It passes, along with the acceptance repro (exit 0). Four mutants were each caught: done put back to true, the how-text paraphrased, a whole-file LF+BOM rewrite that the repro alone accepts, and a touched SmbRig.cs. I did not run the SMB-LOOPBACK test. The engine's own obligation store is not in the tree, so I do not claim this edit routes anything there.

files.why: Line 108 only: O-030 goes from "done": true to "done": false. Its how-text and the other 318 lines are byte-identical: git diff --numstat HEAD reads 1 1, CRLF is kept, and there is no BOM.

M2/M3/m1: added an '*O-030, owed to the person.*' entry to the person-run network check, which is the N-001..N-004 record. It gives the command on one line and about 70 s, says the result goes next to N-001..N-004 and that O-030 is discharged there, says SL-038's O-030 stays done:false as history and is never set true, and says spike#55's 66.2 s pass broke 'No stage runs it' and does not discharge O-030. I also reworded 'StalledShareTests has never passed on the extracted rig' to 'No person has run StalledShareTests on the extracted rig (the one agent run ... does not count)', because the spike's pass had made the old sentence false. numstat: 11 added, 2 removed.

The design names no test for cases C-002..C-005, and the case obligations need one that feeds each shape in. This script only reads files and git, and runs one case with -Case C-00n. C-002: O-030's how-text is byte-identical to base 6c57f0c. C-003: the ledger differs from base in exactly one line (numstat 1 1), has no BOM and uses one line-ending style. C-004: every O-030 state under SL-038 is undischarged, and the SL-020-scanner.md person-run check carries O-030. C-005: every path the slice touched is on an allowlist, and the repro still holds the content the repro stage wrote. It never runs the SMB test.

obligations.how: Owed to validate-slice. I ran `pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tests/bugs/O-030-ledger-discharge.Tests.ps1` after the edit and it exited 0 ('OK: O-030 is correctly recorded as owed to the person, not discharged.'). The repro file is unmodified. Validate still owns the discharge.

C-001 is fed by the unmodified acceptance test tests/bugs/O-030-ledger-discharge.Tests.ps1, which exits 0 now. With done set back to true as a temporary mutant, it exited 1 at line 52. Afterwards I restored the file and checked it was byte-identical by hash.

C-002 is `tests/bugs/SL-062-LedgerCases.ps1 -Case C-002`. It parses O-030 from `git show 6c57f0c:<ledger>` and from the working tree and requires the how-text to be ordinal-equal, both 'NEVER run' and 'remains owed to the person' to be present, and the object to keep the shape {key, done, how}. It passes 6/6. A mutant that only dropped a comma in the how-text failed it.

C-003 is `-Case C-003`. It requires `git diff --numstat 6c57f0c -- <ledger>` to be exactly '1\t1\t<ledger>', no BOM, one line-ending style, the same line count, and exactly one differing line: the one below '"key": "O-030",', going from '"done": true,' to '"done": false,'. It passes 8/8. Mutant 1 (done back to true) failed it. Mutant 3 was a whole-file LF+BOM rewrite with the same meaning. The repro passes that mutant with exit 0, but C-003 failed it on numstat and on the BOM.

C-004 is `-Case C-004`. It walks every JSON under .taad/slices/SL-038/ for objects with key O-030 that carry a done or discharged field. It finds exactly two: build-slice-2.json (done now false) and code-review-2.json (discharged:'no', already right). It requires both to be found and neither to say discharged. index.json has only the key in a revoke list and validate-slice-4.json has only prose, so there was no mirror to flip. It also requires the SL-020-scanner.md person-run check to carry the O-030 entry: the command in full, about 70 s, next to N-001..N-004, discharged there, and the agent run not discharging it. It passes 11/11. Mutant 1 failed it. The engine's DB store is not visible from the tree (see O-007).

C-005 is `-Case C-005`. It gathers this slice's paths from the engine's SL-062 commits plus the uncommitted tree while slice/SL-062 is checked out, so it still means 'this slice' after the merge. It requires every path to be on the allowlist: the ledger, SL-020-scanner.md, the two tests/bugs scripts and .taad/slices/SL-062/. It requires StalledShareTests.cs and Rig/SmbRig.cs to be untouched, and the repro's LF-normalised SHA-256 to be B0DD9D40...FBC4, its content as the repro stage wrote it. It passes 6/6. A mutant that appended CRLF to SmbRig.cs failed it. I did not rerun the SMB-LOOPBACK test.

The only human-facing queue for this item in the tree is docs/design/SL-020-scanner.md's 'person-run network check'. `git grep -i sitting` outside .taad/slices finds nothing, and .taad holds only slices/ and fitness.yaml. O-030 is now on that record, and C-004 checks it is there. The engine's obligation state lives in its own store: build-slice-2.json carries run_id 1047 and is an export of it. That store is outside this worktree and I did not read engine code outside my folder, so I cannot show O-030 in the engine's queue. This is an engine-side gap, filed under follow_ups. I do not claim the done:false flip routes anything in the engine.

`git grep -n N-004 -- .taad docs` found the record at docs/design/SL-020-scanner.md:225-229 ('The person-run network check', which already names StalledShareTests). I added O-030 there by reference, with the command on one line, 'about 70 s', 'owed to the person', and the rule that its result goes next to N-001 to N-004. This is a changed ledger file, listed in files.

I dropped the line 'O-030 can then be set done:true ... in a later slice'. The SL-020-scanner.md entry now says SL-038's own build record keeps O-030 at done:false as history and it is never set true there, and that 'this record is where O-030 is discharged'. So the permanent repro stays consistent with the correct later path. I cannot edit the design record itself, so this is also listed under deviations.

I scoped the search to .taad/slices/SL-038/ and edited only build-slice-2.json there. The O-030 keys in other slices are different, per-slice obligations: SL-024 build-slice-1/2 and code-review-1, SL-044 build-slice-2, code-review-2 and index, SL-047 build-slice-7, code-review-4, index and validate-slice-1/2, and SL-056 validate-slice-1. They are listed and not edited, and C-004 prints them as 'not judged'. `git diff --name-only HEAD` lists only .taad/slices/SL-038/build-slice-2.json and docs/design/SL-020-scanner.md. C-005 enforces the allowlist mechanically.

Stated here and in the SL-020-scanner.md entry: spike#55, an engine stage, ran `--filter Network=SMB-LOOPBACK`, which includes New-SmbMapping. That broke the recorded rule 'No stage runs it' (SL-020-scanner.md:228) and the stack line 'no engine stage runs it'. I ran a read-only `Get-SmbMapping`, with output limited to \\127.0.0.1\ entries, and found 0 loopback mappings, so the spike left none behind. The conflict: the brief says '(validate or the person)', while the stack and SL-020-scanner.md say no stage runs it. The stack wins, so O-030 is owed to the person only, not to validate. The mechanical guard is code, so it is filed as a follow-up and not built.

The O-030 entry in SL-020-scanner.md, which is the record the person reads, cites spike#55: 'ran the command at HEAD 6c57f0c, and 1 of 1 passed in 66.2 s. That run broke "No stage runs it" above and does not discharge O-030.' I also reworded :251-252 from 'has never passed on the extracted rig' to 'No person has run StalledShareTests on the extracted rig (the one agent run ... does not count)', so the record no longer says something the engine measured as false.

Ran `git log -S '"O-008"' -- .taad/slices/SL-038`. The precedent commit is 91c955d (SL-038 build attempt 2). Its shape: O-008 still reads done:true in build-slice-1.json:112 and was never hand-edited. The correction went into the next build record (O-017's how: 'O-008 is partly tested, not discharged') and into SL-020-scanner.md. design-slice-2.json:140 says the split went through the engine's disposition, not a hand-edit. So the design's auth_model ('only in the narrow way the accepted O-008 correction was made') is wrong. This slice matches the precedent's SL-020-scanner.md half. The hand-edit of build-slice-2.json rests on the brief (SL-038 code-review-2.json m1 fix, 'Change the ledger only; no code changes') and on the acceptance test. Recorded in deviations.

Restated rationale: a ConvertFrom-Json/ConvertTo-Json round-trip rewrites formatting across the whole file under either PowerShell, and truncates or re-escapes only under 5.1. The decision stands. The edit was a single anchored text replacement and never a round-trip. Mutant 3 showed that a whole-file rewrite with the same meaning passes the repro and fails C-003. The design record is not mine to edit, so this is in deviations.

`git diff --numstat HEAD` shows '1\t1\t.taad/slices/SL-038/build-slice-2.json' and '11\t2\tdocs/design/SL-020-scanner.md', and no other tracked file. C-003 enforces the 1 1 mechanically against base 6c57f0c. Untracked additions are only the repro, SL-062-LedgerCases.ps1 and the engine's own .taad/slices/SL-062/ records, and C-005 checks that allowlist.

deviations: Hand-off note: the design places it 'at .taad/slices/SL-062/'. I wrote no file there. That directory holds the engine's own records, and the engine writes build-slice-1.json from this output. The note is this output plus, per M2, the O-030 entry in docs/design/SL-020-scanner.md, where the person's check actually lives.

Design contract 'once a person runs it and it passes, O-030 can then be set done:true ... in a later slice' is wrong (M3): no later slice could do that without breaking the permanent repro. It is replaced by: SL-038's O-030 stays done:false as history, and its discharge is recorded in SL-020-scanner.md's person-run network check.

Mirror check: the design used `git grep O-030 -- .taad` and 'flip any mirror'. Per M4 it is scoped to .taad/slices/SL-038/. O-030 in other slices is a different obligation. There, only build-slice-2.json and code-review-2.json carry an O-030 state (the latter already 'no'), so nothing else was flipped.

The design's O-008 precedent is wrong (m2). Commit 91c955d did not hand-edit build-slice-1.json, where O-008 still reads done:true. It corrected O-008 in the next build record and in SL-020-scanner.md. This slice's hand-edit of an engine-exported record rests on the brief (SL-038 code-review-2 m1 fix) and the acceptance test, not on O-008.

Round-trip rationale restated (m3): a ConvertTo-Json round-trip rewrites formatting across the whole file under either PowerShell, and truncates or re-escapes only under Windows PowerShell 5.1. The pwsh 7 claims in the design were stale. The decision is unchanged.

SL-020-scanner.md :251-252 was reworded as well as the O-030 entry being added. It said StalledShareTests 'has never passed on the extracted rig', which spike#55's pass made false (m1). It now says no person has run it.

The design names no test for cases C-002..C-005, so I added tests/bugs/SL-062-LedgerCases.ps1, which only reads files and git. The m4 allowlist `git diff --name-only HEAD` sees only tracked files, so C-005's allowlist also admits the untracked tests/bugs scripts and the engine's .taad/slices/SL-062/ records.
follow_ups: Engine-side obligation (M1): SL-038's obligation state lives in the engine's store (build-slice-2.json is export run_id 1047), and that store still holds O-030 done:true. The hand-edit here does not change the store. A re-export of SL-038 would put done:true back, and it would also turn the repro and C-003 red. The engine needs a way to reopen an obligation on a merged slice through its disposition, and a queue of person-owed items that a slice can read from the tree.

Mechanical guard (M5), code, not built here: the rig should refuse New-SmbMapping unless a person-sitting marker is set, for example an environment variable that only the person sets. Today 'no engine stage runs Network=SMB-LOOPBACK' is kept only by stages remembering it, and spike#55 on this slice did not.

The person's network check is owed: `WindowCases.ps1 -Case All -IncludeNetwork`, then `eng/dotnet.ps1 test tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests.csproj --filter Network=SMB-LOOPBACK` (~70 s). Record the HEAD, pass or fail for N-001..N-004 and StalledShareTests (O-030), and N-001's Cancel-to-return in SL-020-scanner.md. On 2026-09-27 a read-only Get-SmbMapping showed 0 leftover \\127.0.0.1\ mappings.

tests/bugs/SL-062-LedgerCases.ps1 has two anchors. C-002 and C-003 compare against base 6c57f0c, and C-005 pins the repro's content hash. A later slice that edits build-slice-2.json or the repro (which SL-020-scanner.md now says nobody should do) must retire or update these cases in the same commit.

SL-062's design record (design-slice-1.json) still carries the contract line 'O-030 can then be set done:true ... in a later slice' and the O-008 auth_model. Read it together with this build's deviations.
not_built: The SMB-LOOPBACK command itself: it is person-run by contract and changes the machine's SMB mappings. Build did not run it and does not claim it.
Showing O-030 in the engine's own obligation queue (M1): that store is not in this worktree. I recorded this as an engine-side gap and did not claim routing.
The rig's mechanical person-sitting guard (M5): it is code, so it is out of scope for a ledger-only slice and is filed under follow_ups.

tests.note: This is the acceptance oracle. After the edit it exits 0: 'OK: O-030 is correctly recorded as owed to the person, not discharged.' Before the edit, the engine measured exit 1.

First run. My helper `function Git` shadowed `git` (PowerShell names are case-insensitive) and recursed forever inside C-002. The tool moved it to the background, I stopped the pwsh process I had started, and it ended with exit 255. I renamed the helper to Invoke-Git.
Second run: every check held, exit 0. Two messages printed wrongly because the locals $record and $repro overwrote $Record and $Repro (case-insensitive). I renamed the locals and reran.
Final run, alone: 6 ok, 0 FAIL, exit 0.
Final run, alone: 8 ok, 0 FAIL, exit 0. numstat against 6c57f0c is 1 1. The file is CRLF 319, bare LF 0, with no BOM.
Final run, alone: 11 ok, 0 FAIL, exit 0. It finds O-030's state in build-slice-2.json (False) and code-review-2.json ('no'), and lists the other slices' O-030 files without judging them.
Final run, alone: 6 ok, 0 FAIL, exit 0. Paths touched: the ledger, SL-020-scanner.md, the two tests/bugs scripts and .taad/slices/SL-062/*.

tests.command: mutation run: build-slice-2.json with O-030 done back to true, then the repro, -Case C-003 and -Case C-004; restored by bytes
tests.note: All three caught it. The repro exited 1, C-003 failed numstat and the one-line check, and C-004 failed 'done is false'. The restored file's hash matched the original.

tests.command: mutation run: how-text with one comma dropped, then -Case C-002; restored by bytes
tests.note: C-002 failed on the byte-for-byte how-text check with exit 1, which is the intended result. The file was restored.

tests.command: mutation run: whole ledger rewritten as LF + BOM with the same meaning, then the repro and -Case C-003; restored by bytes
tests.note: The repro still exits 0 on this rewrite, which is the m4 point. C-003 caught it on numstat and on the BOM, exit 1. The file was restored with a matching hash.

tests.command: mutation run: CRLF appended to tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/Rig/SmbRig.cs, then -Case C-005; restored by bytes
tests.note: C-005 failed the allowlist check and 'SmbRig.cs is untouched', exit 1. SmbRig.cs was restored with a matching hash, and git status showed only the slice's own changes.
Read-only, and the output was limited to loopback rig mappings: '127.0.0.1 mappings: 0'. spike#55 left no rig mapping behind (M5).
'1\t1\t.taad/slices/SL-038/build-slice-2.json' and '11\t2\tdocs/design/SL-020-scanner.md', and no other tracked file.

This is O-030 itself, person-run by contract. It maps an SMB share on the person's machine, and SL-020-scanner.md:228 says no stage runs it. It is owed to the person's check, where the result is recorded.

The slice changes only a ledger value and a design record, so no app, Core or test code is touched. Nothing in src/, eng/ or the xUnit tests reads either file (grep), so building or launching the WPF app would exercise nothing this slice changed. The way these files are used is the acceptance command and the person reading SL-020-scanner.md, and I ran and checked both.
